Distance Intersection over Union (LD -IoU) localization loss integrated 
into the YOLOv8 framework. B y incorporating the Lorentzian distance into the conventional IoU formulation, the 
proposed loss provides a more robust representation of spatial discrepancy, enabling more accurate bounding -box 
regression. Experiments conducted on the OAI dataset demonstr ate that the proposed framework consistently 
outperforms the baseline YOLOv8 and existing IoU -based localization losses. The proposed LD -IoU-YOLOv8 
achieved 99.1% precision, 94.2% mAP@0.5:0.95, 99.6% mAP@0.5, and 98.8% recall, while reducing the Box Loss 
from 0.291 to 0.093, corresponding to an approximately 68% relative reduction. Furthermore, the proposed localization 
loss demonstrated faster convergence than the conventional IoU loss, achieving high mAP@0.5 in fewer training 
epochs and providing more eff icient

Union (LD-IoU) localization loss is proposed 
to improve bounding -box regression by 
incorporating the Lorentzian distance into the 
conventional IoU formulation, enabling more 
accurate localization and faster optimization 
during training.

YOLOv8 framework and extensively

mAP@0.5 and reducing the Box Loss from

IoU.

the proposed LD-IoU consistently outperforms 
IoU, GIoU, DIoU, CIoU, and SIoU while 
exhibiting demonstrating strong generalization 
across one -stage and two -stage object 
detection fr ameworks, producing tighter and 
more accurate bounding boxes.

carried out based on the publicly availabl e Knee 
Osteoarthritis Severity Dataset obtained from the 
Kaggle repository, which is derived from the original 
Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) database [23]. The 
Kaggle version provides preprocessed knee X -ray 
images annotated according to the Kellgren –
Lawrence (KL) grading system and was used 
throughout this study. Since the publicly available 
Kaggle dataset does not provide patient identifiers or 
subject-level metadata, the primary experiments were 
conducted using an image-level partitioning strategy. 
An additional patient-level evaluation using data with 
available patient identifiers was subsequently 
performed to assess the potential risk of patient-level 
data leakage. Therefore, the dataset was divided into

evidence.excerpt:
localization loss functions 
In order to test the efficacy of the proposed LD -
IoU loss, some more experiments were done using 
the localization loss function of YOLOv8 with other 
popular IoU loss functions. In addition to the 
conventional IoU, GIoU, DIoU, CIoU, and SIoU 
losses, three r ecent IoU -based localization losses, 
namely EIoU, WIoU, and Shape -IoU, were also 
included in the comparison to provide a more 
comprehensive evaluation against recent localization 
methods. All localization loss functions were 
implemented within the same YOL Ov8 architecture 
and evaluated under identical experimental 
conditions, including the same OAI dataset, data split, 
image preprocessing, optimizer, training schedule 
(100 epochs), hyperparameters, and evaluation 
protocol, ensuring a fair head -to-head compa rison. 
All experiments were done using the same OAI 
dataset, network

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Held-out test, external dataset, and patient-level split evaluations all show consistent high performance, with mAP@0.5:0.95 of 92.8% on both the external dataset and the patient-level partition.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO-style object detection metrics (Precision, Recall, mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95) computed on held-out test data, an external knee X-ray dataset, and a patient-level partitioned test set.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised gradient descent using a task loss that combines the proposed LD-IoU regression loss with classification losses on training image partitions.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance gains (e.g., 99.6% mAP@0.5, 94.2% mAP@0.5:0.95, and substantial box loss reduction) are backed by aligned tabular and graphical evidence across comparable baselines, with consistent improvements shown across one-stage and two-stage detector families.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is rigorous and multifaceted: the proposed loss is benchmarked against eight existing IoU-based loss variants (IoU, GIoU, DIoU, CIoU, SIoU, EIoU, WIoU, Shape-IoU) on the OAI dataset, evaluated across 9 different one-stage and two-stage detectors, verified via ablation of distance normalization, statistically analyzed across multiple random seeds with 95% confidence intervals, evaluated on an external dataset, and checked for patient-level split leakage.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations on a held-out test split, an external digital knee X-ray dataset, and a strict patient-level partitioned test set demonstrate consistent high performance (mAP@0.5:0.95 of 92.8% on the external dataset and 92.8% under patient-level partitioning).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard COCO-style object detection evaluation metrics (Precision, Recall, mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95) computed on held-out test datasets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised gradient descent backpropagation using task loss combining LD-IoU regression loss and classification losses on training image partitions.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly address key limitations, noting that initial experiments relied on Kaggle OAI image-level splits, confirming robustness via patient-level splits and external dataset testing, while noting that future work remains needed for larger multi-center cohorts and modalities such as MRI/CT.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly formulated mathematically: the authors define center-point Lorentzian distance, its scale-invariant normalization based on the smallest enclosing bounding box, and its integration into the regression loss. Implementation details, including hyperparameter settings, dataset split protocols, and optimization procedures across Ultralytics YOLOv8 and MMDetection frameworks, are clearly specified.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clearly motivated, mathematically sound, and thoroughly benchmarked localization loss. The extensive comparative evaluation against current state-of-the-art IoU variants and diverse model architectures, along with ablation, multi-seed statistical testing, and data leakage checks, demonstrates scientific rigor justifying admission.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces LD-IoU (Lorentzian Distance Intersection over Union), a scale-invariant bounding-box regression loss function that integrates normalized Lorentzian distance into the standard IoU formulation to improve localization and convergence in YOLOv8 and other object detection frameworks for knee osteoarthritis severity detection.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clearly motivated, mathematically sound, and thoroughly benchmarked localization loss. The extensive comparative evaluation against current state-of-the-art IoU variants and diverse model architectures, along with ablation, multi-seed statistical testing, and data leakage checks, demonstrates scientific rigor justifying admission.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly address key limitations, noting that initial experiments relied on Kaggle OAI image-level splits, confirming robustness via patient-level splits and external dataset testing, while noting that future work remains needed for larger multi-center cohorts and modalities such as MRI/CT.
